stories.headline: Amit Shah speaks to Andhra CM, promises aid over Cyclone Murasu
stories.title: Amit Shah speaks to Andhra CM, promises aid over Cyclone Murasu
stories.summary: Amaravati, Nov 3 : Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu over the phone about the impact of Cyclone ‘Murasu’ which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast early Tuesday. HM Shah assured him of every possible assistance from the Centre. The Union Home Minister said in a post on ‘X’ that NDRF and SDRF teams are already on the ground, helping those affected. He stated that the Government of India stands with the people with an unwavering resolve. The Home Minister inquired about the impact of Cyclone ‘Murasu’. “I assured him that the Central Government will provide all kinds of assistance and support. Already, NDRF and SDRF teams are on the ground, undertaking relief measures and standing as a support for the people in the cyclone-affected areas. The Government of India stands with the people of Andhra Pradesh with a firm resolve to face any kind of situation,” he said. Earlier, Chandrababu Naidu briefed Amit Shah on the situation following Cyclone ‘Arnab’ and the subsequent arrival of Cyclone ‘Murasu’. The Chief Minister explained the crop losses and damage to property reported in various districts. He thanked the Union Minister for sending a central team to assess the damage caused by cyclone ‘Arnab’. The Chief Minister sought adequate assistance from the Centre to help the state recover from the impact of the successive cyclones. Meanwhile, CM Naidu has thanked Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and the people of Karnataka for standing with Andhra Pradesh during Cyclone Murasu. The Andhra Pradesh CM posted on ‘X’ that their timely support in our hour of need will never be forgotten." CM Shivakumar had earlier posted about the help being extended to Andhra Pradesh. “Our teams are on their way to Andhra Pradesh to support relief and restoration efforts in the cyclone-affected areas. Karnataka stands with the people of Andhra Pradesh, and we will extend every possible support during this difficult time,” the Karnataka Chief Minister said. Shivakumar had posted earlier that he spoke to Chandrababu Naidu and assured him of Karnataka’s full support as Andhra Pradesh grapples with the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab. “With over 15,000 electricity poles uprooted by Arnab, the restoration of power infrastructure is critical, and Andhra Pradesh has sought Karnataka’s assistance in this effort. Our Energy Department is coordinating the assistance, with Energy Minister Shri K.J. George closely monitoring the situation.” He revealed that Karnataka is deploying 500 skilled men, along with the necessary equipment, to expedite restoration works and facilitate the early restoration of electricity supply in the cyclone-affected areas. --IANS

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu Nov. 3 | Red alert lifted from two Telangana districts; issued for Suryapet, Khammam and Bhadradri
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu Nov. 3 | Red alert lifted from two Telangana districts; issued for Suryapet, Khammam and Bhadradri
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Three districts in Telangana were placed under red alert — indicating possibility of heavy to very heavy with isolated extremely heavy rain — on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), under the impact of the severe cyclonic storm Murasu (war drum).
The eye of the storm crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast at 5.30 a.m.

While Nalgonda and Nagakurnool were earlier placed under the weather alert, India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre on Tuesday has forecast heavy to very heavy with isolated extremely heavy rain in Suryapet, Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts.
Only Mahabubabad was placed under orange alert, meaning heavy to very heavy rain, as per the IMD’s impact based rainfall bulletin issued in the afternoon.
Moderate to heavy rain was forecast in Nalgonda, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Jangaon, Hanumakonda, Warangal and Mulugu.

Till 12.00 p.m., the highest of 25.5 mm rain was recorded in Madhira of Khammam, followed by 22.8mm in Sathupalle and 20 mm in Vemsoor, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s State rainfall data.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu delays winter in Bengal, relief expected before Kali Puja
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu delays winter in Bengal, relief expected before Kali Puja
stories.summary: Cyclone Murasu's indirect impact delays the onset of winter in West Bengal, with temperatures expected to dip before Kali Puja on November 8 as rainfall subsides and skies clear.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Murasu's indirect impact delays the onset of winter in West Bengal, with temperatures expected to dip before Kali Puja on November 8 as rainfall subsides and skies clear.

Kolkata: The indirect impact of Cyclone Murasu has delayed the onset of winter in West Bengal, with temperatures remaining above normal across the state, the meteorological department said on Tuesday.
However, weather conditions are expected to improve from Thursday (November 5), with temperatures likely to dip ahead of Kali Puja on November 8, bringing the much-awaited winter chill to the state.
According to the weather department, scattered rainfall is likely in several parts of Bengal on Tuesday under the influence of Cyclone Murasu, which made landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
The cyclone has triggered forecasts of heavy rainfall, with a red alert issued for coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu.
Although Bengal is unlikely to experience any direct impact of the cyclone, its indirect effects are expected to influence weather conditions.
The sky will remain partly cloudy across all districts on Tuesday, with isolated spells of light rain.
In north Bengal, Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri, Kalimpong, Alipurduar and Cooch Behar may receive light rainfall at one or two places.
The remaining three districts of north Bengal are expected to remain dry.

In south Bengal, isolated light to moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms is likely in North 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas, Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly, East Midnapore, West Midnapore, Jhargram, Bankura and Purulia.
Other districts are likely to experience predominantly dry weather.
The meteorological department has forecast mainly dry conditions across the state from Wednesday to Saturday, with the possibility of rainfall gradually diminishing.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu: A.P. CM calls for efforts to prevent loss of lives
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu: A.P. CM calls for efforts to prevent loss of lives
stories.summary: In a teleconference with senior officials in the State administration, and District Collectors, Mr. Naidu advised the people to follow government advisories till the cyclone withers away
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Keeping a tab of the cyclone Murasu, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu instructed the officials to do all that is possible to prevent loss of lives, and to focus on drinking water and power supply and road connectivity.
In a teleconference with senior officials in the State administration, and District Collectors, Mr. Naidu advised the people to follow government advisories till the cyclone withers away.
Officials told the CM that the cyclone made landfall near Ongole, where it uprooted several trees, and there was widespread waterlogging in agricultural fields in Nellore district.
They further apprised the CM that power supply was disrupted at many places in Palnadu, Markapur and Guntur districts, and restoration works were in progress.

Mr. Naidu said the cyclone effect was likely to subside fully by November 3 night and that the next four to five hours were crucial as more rains were expected in Bapatla, Guntur, Prakasam, Palnadu, Krishna, NTR, Eluru and West Godavari districts.
He ordered that restoration works be taken up on a war - footing in Prakasam and Bapatla districts which were badly affected, while encouraging the efforts being made to mitigate the cyclone impact.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu: Kerala braces for heavy rains; evacuations in Andhra’s Prakasam
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu: Kerala braces for heavy rains; evacuations in Andhra’s Prakasam
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Kerala braces for heavy indirect rainfall as Severe Cyclone Murasu prompts emergency evacuations across coastal Prakasam.

Ongole (Andhra Pradesh): Kerala is set to receive widespread indirect rainfall as Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu approaches the southern Andhra Pradesh coastline, prompting local authorities in Prakasam district to launch massive evacuation drives and step up disaster preparedness.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) confirmed that while Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu is positioned off the south Andhra Pradesh coast, its indirect system will trigger increased rainfall across Kerala over the coming days.

IMD scientist Neetha K Gopal noted that a cyclonic circulation off the Kerala coast and easterly wave troughs will bring light to moderate rain across most parts of Kerala, with isolated heavy rainfall in several districts.
As the storm system moves closer, crosses the coast and dissipates, enhanced precipitation will continue over Kerala through the weekend without severe coastal hazards.
Meanwhile, in Prakasam district, rising tides and strong winds have already begun impacting the coastline.
District Collector P Raja Babu announced that 26 vulnerable villages across seven coastal mandals were identified for immediate evacuation.
High-risk groups, including children, elderly residents and pregnant women, nearing delivery dates, were relocated to safe shelters and nearby hospitals.
To safeguard the 74-kilometre coastal belt of Prakasam, three National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams were deployed alongside local revenue and police personnel.
Round-the-clock command control rooms have been activated across mandal, divisional and district levels to monitor field feedback.

stories.headline: J&K Consumer Commission Holds Bajaj Allianz Liable For Unjustified Deduction From Flood Insurance Claim
stories.title: J&K Consumer Commission Holds Bajaj Allianz Liable For Unjustified Deduction From Flood Insurance Claim
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Jammu and Kashmir State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Srinagar, comprising President (Officiating) Nighat Sultana and Member Maheep Gupta, has held Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd.
liable for deficiency in service after it deducted a portion of an insurance claim despite the surveyor assessing the flood-related losses at a higher amount.

The Commission found that the insurer failed to produce documentary evidence supporting the deductions or establishing the complainant's consent to a negotiated settlement and directed it to pay the differential claim amount along with compensation for delay and litigation costs.
The complainant, Showkat Ahmad Mir, a resident of Batapora, Khanabal, Anantnag, filed a consumer complaint against Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd.
and Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd., alleging deficiency in service over the settlement of an insurance claim arising from flood damage to his insured business unit.
The complainant stated that his business unit suffered losses due to floods during the currency of the insurance policy.
The loss was assessed by the insurance company's surveyor, Tahir Ahmad Shah, at ₹44,56,374 through an assessment report dated June 16, 2015.
The insurance company subsequently settled the claim in May 2017 by paying ₹36.90 lakh to the complainant.

Aggrieved by the deduction of ₹7,66,374 from the surveyor-assessed loss, the complainant approached the Jammu and Kashmir State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Srinagar, seeking payment of the deducted amount, along with interest at 12.40%, compensation of ₹1.50 lakh for unfair trade practices and ₹50,000 towards litigation expenses.
The insurance company contended that the complainant had been asked to submit sale and purchase bills, VAT returns and other supporting documents but had opted for a negotiated settlement instead.
It claimed that he had agreed to accept ₹37 lakh as full and final settlement and submitted a discharge voucher.
After deducting a reinstatement premium of ₹10,000, the company paid ₹36.90 lakh through a cheque dated May 22, 2017.

stories.headline: 'Govt, private sectors must come forward to make Delhi a medical hub’: CM Gupta
stories.title: 'Govt, private sectors must come forward to make Delhi a medical hub’: CM Gupta
stories.summary: Recalling the hospital's contribution during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Chief Minister said its doctors, employees and management continued to discharge their responsibilities during the difficult period.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Recalling the hospital's contribution during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Chief Minister said its doctors, employees and management continued to discharge their responsibilities during the difficult period.

New Delhi: Delhi Chief Minister, Rekha Gupta, on Tuesday said that both the government and private sectors would have to work together to transform the national Capital into a medical hub, while stressing the need to strengthen healthcare infrastructure and ensure quality treatment facilities for everyone.
The Chief Minister was speaking after inaugurating an IVF centre at a private hospital in Delhi.
She said the government was working towards ensuring that anyone coming to the national Capital could access proper medical treatment and healthcare facilities.
"If we truly want to make Delhi a medical hub, both the government and private sectors will have to come forward.
According to WHO parameters, at least five medical beds should be available for every 1,000 people.
Our country is still behind this benchmark, and I believe Delhi currently has around two beds per 1,000 people," Gupta said.
She emphasised that achieving the target of five beds per 1,000 people would require coordinated efforts from both sectors.
"To make it reach up to five beds, both sectors are required to work together.
If anybody comes to Delhi, they must get proper treatment and health facilities.
This is the Prime Minister's dream, and the Delhi government is working in that direction," she added.
Praising the contribution of the private hospital to healthcare services in the national Capital, Gupta said the institution had served lakhs of people and saved countless lives over the years.

stories.headline: India, Israel vote against UNGA draft on regional conventional arms control
stories.title: India, Israel vote against UNGA draft on regional conventional arms control
stories.summary: United Nations, Nov 03: India and Israel have voted against a draft resolution in the UN by Pakistan and Belarus on conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels, with New Delhi saying countries' security concerns are not confined within regional boundaries. The draft resolution, titled ‘General and complete disarmament: Conventional arms control at the regional and subregional levels’, was approved by the UN General Assembly’s First Committee on Monday with 180 votes in favour, two against and no abstentions. India and Israel were the only countries to vote against the resolution in the 193-member UN body. Explaining India's vote, First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the UN, Anmol Sher Bedi said conventional arms control was a global issue. “We are not fully convinced that it should be pursued primarily in regional and sub-regional contexts,” Bedi said while delivering India’s Explanation of Vote in the UNGA First Committee. He said New Delhi voted against the resolution consistent with its past position. India also questioned the resolution's request to the UN Disarmament Commission to consider formulating principles that could serve as a framework for regional agreements on conventional arms control. “We read this request with a certain degree of curiosity,” Bedi said. stories.headline: Indian national from Tamil Nadu dies in Nepal helicopter crash
stories.title: Indian national from Tamil Nadu dies in Nepal helicopter crash
stories.summary: Kathmandu, Nov 3 : The foreign national killed in a helicopter collision in Nepal on Tuesday has been identified as an Indian, officials said. One person was killed and another injured when two helicopters collided in the mountainous Solukhumbu district of eastern Nepal on Tuesday morning. Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Nabin Raja Budhathoki, chief of the District Police Office in Solukhumbu, told IANS that Vasanth Kumar, an Indian national from Tamil Nadu, was killed in the accident. "The injured person is a New Zealand national of Indian origin," he said. Both were passengers aboard a Fishtail Air helicopter that collided with an Air Dynasty helicopter as the two helicopters attempted to land at a helipad in the Pheriche area of Solukhumbu district on Tuesday morning, according to preliminary reports. Budhathoki said the pilot of the Fishtail Air helicopter also sustained minor injuries. However, the Air Dynasty helicopter had no passengers on board, Nepali authorities said. The Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal said in a press release that an AS350 helicopter operated by Air Dynasty Heli Service Pvt. Ltd., registration number 9NAOD, had departed from Lukla Airport for Pheriche. The other helicopter, an AS350 operated by Fishtail Air Pvt. Ltd., registration number 9NAJR, had departed from the Gorakshep area for Pheriche carrying two foreign nationals. The two helicopters collided while landing at Pheriche at 8:12 a.m. local time, the authority said. Videos circulating on social media appear to show the rotor blades of the two helicopters colliding as the aircraft approached each other, before they fell to the ground. Local media reports said the injured passenger had been brought to Kathmandu for further treatment. "We are preparing to send the body of the passenger killed in the accident to Kathmandu for a post-mortem examination," Budhathoki said. The Everest region is a major tourist destination, and helicopters operate frequently in the area, transporting foreign tourists and supporting rescue operations. --IANS

stories.title: Telangana’s Rs 30,000-crore drought relief plea hits Delhi roadblock
stories.summary: Telangana's Congress government failed to secure a concrete Centre's assurance on its proposed Rs 30,000-crore drought relief package despite a three-day Delhi visit by Chief Minister Revanth Reddy and Cabinet Ministers, while farmers continue facing drought-related crop losses
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Hyderabad: The Congress government’s much-publicised campaign for a Rs 30,000-crore drought relief package yielded little beyond a formal representation.
Chief Minister.

A Revanth Reddy and more than half his Cabinet spent three days in Delhi, announcing plans to seek the intervention of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, but failed to secure a meeting with either of them or the Union Ministers concerned.
While the Chief Minister and his Ministers participated in Congress protests in the national capital, the State’s demand for drought relief remained confined to official channels.
No concrete assurance on the special package emerged, exposing the gap between the government’s political projection and its actual achievement.
The government’s handling of the drought has also come under scrutiny in comparison with neighbouring Andhra Pradesh.
Recording a higher rainfall deficit, Andhra Pradesh moved ahead of Telangana in declaring drought-affected areas and securing a Central assessment.
It declared 388 mandals drought-hit on October 1, well before the October 31 deadline.
A Central team has been deputed to assess the situation, with its visit scheduled for this week.
Telangana declared 365 mandals drought-affected only on October 27.
No Central assessment team has been deputed so far.

Official sources indicated that Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh faced more severe rainfall deficits than Telangana’s 17 per cent shortfall, raising questions over the government’s case for exceptional assistance.

stories.headline: Centre's FY27 fiscal deficit may exceed Budget target by ₹1.2 lakh crore, reach 4.7% of GDP: SBI Research
stories.title: Centre's FY27 fiscal deficit may exceed Budget target by ₹1.2 lakh crore, reach 4.7% of GDP: SBI Research
stories.summary: The report estimates that the fiscal deficit could rise to 4.7% of GDP, compared with the budgeted 4.3%
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Centre's fiscal deficit for 2026-27 could exceed the Budget Estimate by around ₹1.2 lakh crore, with higher subsidy spending and lower tax receipts adding pressure on government finances, according to a report by SBI Research.
The report estimates that the fiscal deficit could rise to 4.7 per cent of GDP, compared with the budgeted 4.3 per cent.
The revised estimate uses the 2022-23 GDP base, while the Budget Estimate was calculated using the 2011-12 base.
SBI Research attributed the increase to structural factors and the impact of the revised GDP base.

The estimated pressure includes a revenue loss of ₹1.1 lakh crore due to the excise duty cut, an additional ₹90,000 crore in fertiliser subsidy and around ₹48,000 crore in petroleum and LPG subsidies.
SBI Research said the government could manage the higher deficit through a combination of stronger cash balances and expenditure cuts, without necessarily increasing its borrowing programme.

"The only possible option with Government to contain fiscal deficit within Budget Estimates is to cut in expenditure," the report said, adding that the average expenditure reduction over the last three years was around ₹45,000 crore.
The report estimated the government's cash balance, adjusted for core liquidity, at around ₹8.5 lakh crore at the end of October 2026, compared with ₹2.2 lakh crore a year earlier.
It expects the balance to moderate to around ₹2.5 lakh crore by the end of March 2027.

Government borrowings have already declined by ₹1.23 lakh crore due to switches and buybacks, bringing the current borrowing estimate to ₹15.97 lakh crore against the budgeted ₹17.2 lakh crore, the report said.
The pressure on government finances is also visible in the first half of FY27.
The fiscal deficit rose 24.7 per cent year-on-year to ₹7.14 lakh crore, while total expenditure increased 10.7 per cent.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Gives Last Opportunity To States To Provide Information Sought By Centre In Prison Discrimination Case
stories.title: Supreme Court Gives Last Opportunity To States To Provide Information Sought By Centre In Prison Discrimination Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today (November 3) expressed its disappointment that 23 States/Union Territories (UTs) are yet to respond to the information sought by the Union Home Ministry in the suo motu case on caste-based discrimination inside prisons.
It has, therefore, given them one last opportunity to respond.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Manmohan warned that if the States/UTs fail to respond by the next date of hearing (January 13), it would be “compelled to direct the Chief Secretaries/Principal Secretaries of all the States/UTs to personally remain present before this Court.” The observations were made while hearing the matter (In Re: Discrimination Inside Prisons in India) in which Senior Advocate (Dr) S Muralidhar is appointed as the Amicus Curiae.
The case arose from the Supreme Court's judgment in Sukanya Shantha v Union of India and Others, wherein directions were issued to address caste-based discrimination in prisons.
The Court later took up this suo motu cognizance to monitor the compliance.

In July this year, the Court took on record a detailed Status Report which showed the written responses still awaited from several States/UTs on the method of collection and transmission of caste data to the NCRB; deletion of caste columns in all prison registers and forms; outsourcing of cleaning work; compliance with the guidelines in Arnesh Kumar and Amanatullah Khan; notifications constituting Boards of Visitors district-wise; the status of new Acts/Rules/Manuals proposed by States/UTs; and the status of amendments to offending provisions in the Acts/Rules/Manuals.
The Court had asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati to take up the matter with all States/UTs and gather the information at the earliest.
Muralidhar also apprised the Court that no State/UT had constituted a Board of Visitors (BoVs) district-wise, as directed in July this year.
It had directed all State Governments/UTs to constitute district-wise BoVs, headed by the Principal District Judge of that particular District, within a period of four weeks from the date of order.
In September this year, the Court noted some progress in constituting the BoVs.
It was informed that only a few districts of different States had constituted them.
Today, the bench took serious note of the non-compliance and warned for personal presence of the officials if the report is not filed by the next date of hearing.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Upholds Condonation Of 423-Day Delay In Plea To Set Aside Ex Parte Decree On Condition To Deposit Rs 75 Lakh
stories.title: Supreme Court Upholds Condonation Of 423-Day Delay In Plea To Set Aside Ex Parte Decree On Condition To Deposit Rs 75 Lakh
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has recently upheld a Madras High Court Division Bench's order condoning a delay of 423 days in filing an application under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) to set aside an ex-parte decree.

It also modified the condition imposed for condonation, holding that the Rs 75,000 which was directed to be paid to the plaintiff must instead be deposited with the High Court, subject to the final outcome of the proceedings.
A bench of Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Justice Atul S Chandurkar ruled so while disposing of two cross-appeals.
One was filed challenging the condition imposed, and the other was filed against the condonation of delay.

The plaintiff (Integrated Finance Company Limited) claimed to have entered into several hire-purchase agreements and a lease agreement with partnership firm Business India (Defendant 1/D1) represented by Defendant Nos. 2 to 4 (D2 to D4).
It filed a recovery suit for Rs 21,88,11,451.96 in March 2010, with future interest at 36%.

Despite service, the defendants did not appear before the trial court (Single Judge of the Madras High Court), and Defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 4 were set ex-parte in August 2021, while Defendant No. 3 (D3) had died in the meantime.
The suit was decreed in November 2021.

The Single Judge dismissed the application seeking condonation of delay in March 2023, finding that D4 had appeared through counsel and filed a common affidavit with the other defendants, and knew about the suit before it was decreed.
In appeal, D4 also urged that he was under bona fide belief that the second defendant was looking after the proceedings and that the claim was being settled.
In August 2024, the Division Bench held that his bona fides in filing the application belatedly could not be doubted, though he had failed to act with due diligence.

article_sentences: The India vs Pakistan match in the Men’s ODI World Cup 2027 has attracted nearly 84 lakh ticket applications, the organisers said on Monday.
The ODI World Cup returns to Africa after 23 years and will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
India and Pakistan will face off on October 10 at Johannesburg’s Wanderers stadium, which has a capacity of just 34,000 spectators.
The same venue will host the final on November 21 – a match that trails close behind with almost eight million ticket requests.
The fixture between India and Pakistan has been one of the most highly anticipated matches in the cricket calendar and the most lucrative financially.
However, India has dominated the fixture, winning in their last nine meetings.
Nearly three million fans from 193 countries have applied for tickets in the ballot window, which remains open until November 21.
More than 120 million total ticket requests have been received for the 14-team showcase that runs October 2 to November 21.

stories.headline: NSA Doval holds talks with Vietnamese ministers, discusses ways to boost security cooperation
stories.title: NSA Doval holds talks with Vietnamese ministers, discusses ways to boost security cooperation
stories.summary: Hanoi, Nov 03: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval on Monday held separate high-level talks with Vietnam's ministers of public security and foreign affairs on strengthening bilateral cooperation in security and other areas and agreed to further enhance the existing "multifaceted" ties. Doval held delegation-level talks with Minister of Public Security General Luong Tam Quang on ongoing cooperation in the security domain, reflecting the "deep and mutually trusted civilisational partnership between India and Vietnam," the Indian Embassy in Hanoi said in a post on X. "Both sides discussed ongoing cooperation in the security domain and agreed to further enhance the existing multifaceted ties. They also exchanged views on regional and global developments," the post said. Separately, Doval also met Vietnam's Foreign Affairs Minister Le Hoai Trung, during which the two sides discussed ways to commemorate the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between the two countries. "2027 marks the 55th anniversary of establishment of diplomatic relations between India and Viet Nam. Both sides discussed ways to commemorate this historic milestone in the spirit of India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," the Indian embassy said in a post. Earlier, Doval met Vietnam's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence General Phan Van Giang and reviewed ongoing bilateral defence cooperation and agreed to further deepen engagement in the sector. "National Security Advisor of India Ajit Doval met today with General Phan Van Giang, Member of the Politburo of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence of Vietnam," the embassy said. "Both sides reviewed the status of ongoing bilateral defence cooperation and agreed to continue further strengthening activities in this field," it said. Doval also visited the historic Quan Su Pagoda in Hanoi on Monday. "He was received by Most Venerable Thich Thanh Nhieu, Standing Vice President and the Chief Abbot of the Pagoda, and Most Venerable Thich Duc Thien, Vice President and Secretary General of the National Viet Nam Buddhist Sangha (VBS)," the Indian embassy said, highlighting Buddhism as a "civilisational bridge" between the people of India and Vietnam. Doval arrived in Vietnam on Sunday on an official visit. His visit is in line with the India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. During Vietnamese President To Lam's visit to India in May, India and Vietnam elevated their ties to an enhanced comprehensive strategic partnership and set a USD 25 billion annual trade target by 2030. Security cooperation remains a key pillar of this upgraded partnership.
